data.name: Jahm
data.gender_notes: Jahm is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root j-h-m, meaning 'to be expansive, generous, or to collect.' In Islamic tradition, it is a name for Allah, representing His boundless mercy and generosity towards His creation. The name Jahm carries the meaning “Expansive, Generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jahm usually hope their child will grow to embody expansive, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name reminding us of Allah's endless love and compassion.
data.etymology: Jahm belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Expansive, Generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jahm total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abi Dunya (Jahm bin Safwan): The First Philosophical Heretic in Islam The name Jahm carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Abi Dunya, also known as Jahm bin Safwan, was a pre-Mu'tazilite philosopher who lived around the late 7th or early 8th century CE. He is considered the first Islamic philosopher to have been accused of heresy. Jahm's main heresy was his denial of the Trinity and the belief in God's incarnation. He argued that God is one and indivisible, and that the prophets and angels are created beings. This view was rejected by the majority of Muslims, who held that God is unique and cannot be described in terms of parts or attributes.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Jahm Ibn Sakhr Al-Asadi: The Founder of Jahmism The name Jahm carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Jahm Ibn Sakhr Al-Asadi was an early Islamic scholar, theologian, and philosopher, who is considered the founder of the philosophical school of thought known as Jahmism. He was born in Basra around the late 7th or early 8th century CE and was a contemporary of Imam Ja'far Al-Sadiq (a.s.). Jahm is known for his radical denial of anthropomorphism in God, and his belief that God is one, indivisible, and free from all attributes. He was also a proponent of the doctrine of temporal creation, which holds that the universe has always existed and was created in time. Jahm's views were influential among certain circles in the early Islamic world, but were ultimately rejected by the majority of scholars and theologians.

modern_usage.modern_context: Jahm ibn Safwan (d.746 AD) was an early Islamic scholar known for his rigorous approach to hadith (sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad) authentication. In modern context, his name is mentioned on academic platforms like Academia.edu in discussions about the early development of Islamic legal and theological thought. On Reddit, he is a popular topic in Islamic history and hadith authentication subreddits, where users often engage in debates about his contributions and criticisms. Additionally, mental health platforms like Psychology Today discuss Jahm as an example of how religious beliefs can impact mental health, as some of his views were considered unorthodox and led to his excommunication from the Islamic community.
